- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

# Downloads page: OS detection, mobile "coming soon", fun interactions, benefits copy ## Context `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx` already has a solid downloads page: a 3-card desktop grid (macOS/Windows/Linux) linking to `/download/[platform]` (a GitHub-releases redirect endpoint), a "web/PWA" callout, a data-portability checklist, and release notes. It's missing what the user asked for: 1. Detecting the visitor's OS and surfacing the right download instead of making them scan three identical cards. 2. A visible "coming soon" section for mobile apps (iOS/Android) — currently absent entirely. 3. More personality/delight in the interactions — currently static. 4. A clearer, more persuasive explanation of *why* someone would want the desktop app over just using the browser — currently one paragraph + a generic checklist that's really about local-first data, not about desktop-vs-browser. This is a single-file, presentation-layer change (plus reusing an existing asset). No backend/Convex work needed — confirmed no waitlist/email-capture mechanism exists in the codebase, so mobile "coming soon" will be informational only (no signup form), consistent with the site's existing `mailto:support@twyne.love` pattern already used on this page. ## Approach All changes are in `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx`. ### 1. OS detection (client-only, progressive enhancement) - Add a `useSignal<"macos" | "windows" | "linux" | null>(null)` for the detected platform. - Add a `useVisibleTask$` that runs once on the client, parsing `navigator.userAgentData?.platform` (modern Chromium) with fallback to `navigator.userAgent`/`navigator.platform` string sniffing (mac/win/linux tokens) — same alias set already defined server-side in `download/[platform]/index.ts` (`PLATFORM_ALIASES`), just mirrored client-side since we can't import a server route module into a browser task. - SSR renders the plain 3-card grid (no layout shift, no flash of wrong content); once hydrated and detected, the matching card gets a highlighted state — no reordering of the DOM (avoids layout jank), just a visual treatment change. ### 2. Highlight the detected platform card - Reuse the existing `/approval-stamp.svg` + `.stamp-tilt` rubber-stamp motif already used on the landing page (`landing-broadsheet.tsx`, `landing-quarterly.tsx`) for a "Recommended" stamp on the detected card — this keeps the fun/playful bit on-brand with the editorial/broadsheet aesthetic rather than introducing a generic UI badge. - Add a small line above the grid that fills in once detection completes, e.g. "Looks like you're on **macOS**." with a typewriter-style fade-in (matches the site's `--font-typewriter` motif), staying blank/generic during SSR. ### 3. Mobile "coming soon" section - New `

Mobile apps

` section (added to the `toc` array too) with two cards (iOS, Android) styled like the desktop cards but visually "stamped" as coming soon (reuse the same stamp asset, rotated the other way via `.stamp-tilt-r`, with text "Coming soon" instead of "Recommended"). - Buttons are disabled/inert (no fake download link), with a short note pointing interested users to `mailto:support@twyne.love` to hear when it ships — consistent with existing support contact pattern on this page, no new form/backend. ### 4. Expand "why desktop over browser" copy - Replace/expand the single intro paragraph under "Desktop app" with a short benefits list grounded in what's actually true in the codebase (`desktop/main.ts`, `electrobun.config.ts`): - Distraction-free native window — no browser tabs/address bar around your writing. - Deep-link ATProto sign-in via the registered `twyne://` URL scheme (smoother OAuth callback than a browser redirect). - Its own dock/taskbar icon and app-switcher entry, separate from your browser. - Same account, sync, and hosted AI as the web — nothing to reconfigure switching between them. - Keep the existing "Your data travels with you" section as-is (it's about local-first/export, a distinct point). ## Files touched - `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx` — all changes above (detection logic, new styles via `useStylesScoped$`, new mobile section, expanded copy, updated `toc`). ## Verification - Run the dev server (`just` / existing dev script) and open `/downloads/` in Chrome via the claude-in-chrome tool. - Confirm SSR/initial render shows the plain grid with no flash, then after hydration the browser's OS gets stamped "Recommended" and the intro line fills in. - Spot-check by spoofing `navigator.userAgentData`/`userAgent` in devtools (or just visually confirm on the current Linux host that the Linux card gets recommended). - Confirm the mobile section renders two "coming soon" stamped cards with inert buttons and a working `mailto:` link. - Check responsive layout at mobile width (existing `.dl-grid` breakpoint at 720px) still holds with the added section.

import { defineSchema, defineTable } from "convex/server";
import { v } from "convex/values";

export default defineSchema({
  // ── Per-user state, synced from the browser on sign-up and on every change. ──
  briefs: defineTable({
    userId: v.string(),
    brief: v.any(),
    updatedAt: v.number(),
  }).index("by_userId", ["userId"]),

  folios: defineTable({
    userId: v.string(),
    folios: v.array(v.any()),
    updatedAt: v.number(),
  }).index("by_userId", ["userId"]),

  folioContent: defineTable({
    userId: v.string(),
    folioId: v.string(),
    html: v.string(),
    updatedAt: v.number(),
  })
    .index("by_userId", ["userId"])
    .index("by_userId_folioId", ["userId", "folioId"]),

  customPersonas: defineTable({
    userId: v.string(),
    personas: v.array(v.any()),
    updatedAt: v.number(),
  }).index("by_userId", ["userId"]),

  // ── Persona feedback notes — the room's marginalia, persisted per user. ──
  // Stored server-side so a signed-in user can re-read their notes across
  // devices. Brief is denormalized so the panel can render summaries cheaply.
  personaNotes: defineTable({
    userId: v.string(),
    noteId: v.string(),
    personaId: v.string(),
    personaName: v.string(),
    personaColor: v.string(),
    type: v.union(
      v.literal("encouragement"),
      v.literal("suggestion"),
      v.literal("critique"),
      v.literal("perspective"),
    ),
    feedback: v.string(),
    anchor: v.optional(v.string()),
    briefTitle: v.optional(v.string()),

/**
 * Export and import for the manuscript. Each format is intentionally
 * a small pure function — no I/O, no UI. The UI layer calls these to
 * produce a `Blob` for download, or to turn an uploaded file into HTML
 * the editor can consume.
 *
 * The shapes match the standard.horse / leaflet.pub convention: a
 * plain markdown file is the canonical share format, with a Twyne
 * backup (`.twyne.json`) that round-trips the brief + folios + content
 * for the cases where the user wants everything back.
 */

import { marked } from "marked";
import type { Folio, LayoutSettings, ProjectBrief, PersonaFeedback } from "../types";
import { DEFAULT_LAYOUT, resolveMargins } from "../types";
import {
  formatCitation,
  type BibEntry,
  type CitationStyle,
} from "./bibliography";

export type ExportFormat = "markdown" | "html" | "txt" | "twyne-backup";

/* ── HTML helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */

export function stripHtml(html: string): string {
  return html
    .replace(/<style[\s\S]*?<\/style>/gi, " ")
    .replace(/<script[\s\S]*?<\/script>/gi, " ")
    .replace(/<\/(p|h[1-6]|li|blockquote|tr|div)>/gi, "\n")
    .replace(/<br\s*\/?>(?=)/gi, "\n")
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ")
    .replace(/ /g, " ")
    .replace(/&/g, "&")
    .replace(/</g, "<")
    .replace(/>/g, ">")
    .replace(/"/g, '"')
    .replace(/'/g, "'")
    .replace(/[ \t]+/g, " ")
    .replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n")

# Downloads page: OS detection, mobile "coming soon", fun interactions, benefits copy ## Context `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx` already has a solid downloads page: a 3-card desktop grid (macOS/Windows/Linux) linking to `/download/[platform]` (a GitHub-releases redirect endpoint), a "web/PWA" callout, a data-portability checklist, and release notes. It's missing what the user asked for: 1. Detecting the visitor's OS and surfacing the right download instead of making them scan three identical cards. 2. A visible "coming soon" section for mobile apps (iOS/Android) — currently absent entirely. 3. More personality/delight in the interactions — currently static. 4. A clearer, more persuasive explanation of *why* someone would want the desktop app over just using the browser — currently one paragraph + a generic checklist that's really about local-first data, not about desktop-vs-browser. This touches the frontend (`src/routes/downloads/index.tsx`) plus a small new Convex backend piece: the user confirmed the mobile "coming soon" section should have a real waitlist (email capture), not just a mailto link — there's no existing waitlist mechanism in the codebase, so this adds one. ## Approach All changes are in `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx`. ### 1. OS detection (client-only, progressive enhancement) - Add a `useSignal<"macos" | "windows" | "linux" | null>(null)` for the detected platform. - Add a `useVisibleTask$` that runs once on the client, parsing `navigator.userAgentData?.platform` (modern Chromium) with fallback to `navigator.userAgent`/`navigator.platform` string sniffing (mac/win/linux tokens) — same alias set already defined server-side in `download/[platform]/index.ts` (`PLATFORM_ALIASES`), just mirrored client-side since we can't import a server route module into a browser task. - SSR renders the plain 3-card grid (no layout shift, no flash of wrong content); once hydrated and detected, the matching card gets a highlighted state — no reordering of the DOM (avoids layout jank), just a visual treatment change. ### 2. Highlight the detected platform card - Reuse the existing `/approval-stamp.svg` + `.stamp-tilt` rubber-stamp motif already used on the landing page (`landing-broadsheet.tsx`, `landing-quarterly.tsx`) for a "Recommended" stamp on the detected card — this keeps the fun/playful bit on-brand with the editorial/broadsheet aesthetic rather than introducing a generic UI badge. - Add a small line above the grid that fills in once detection completes, e.g. "Looks like you're on **macOS**." with a typewriter-style fade-in (matches the site's `--font-typewriter` motif), staying blank/generic during SSR. ### 3. Mobile "coming soon" section with a real waitlist - New `

Mobile apps

` section (added to the `toc` array too) with two cards (iOS, Android) styled like the desktop cards but visually "stamped" as coming soon (reuse the same stamp asset, rotated the other way via `.stamp-tilt-r`, with text "Coming soon" instead of "Recommended"). - Each card has an inline email input + "Notify me" button (no disabled/fake download link — this is the real CTA for mobile). **Backend (new):** - `convex/schema.ts` — add a `waitlist` table: `{ email: string, platform: v.union(v.literal("ios"), v.literal("android")), createdAt: number }`, indexed `by_email_platform` on `["email", "platform"]` for dedupe lookups. - `convex/waitlist.ts` — new file, one public mutation `join({ email, platform })`: - Validate `email` is a plausible address (simple regex — same bar as other client-facing forms in this codebase; no external verification service). - Rate-limit via the existing `consumeRateLimit` helper (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts`, same helper used in `convex/research.ts`), e.g. `{ action: "waitlist:join", identifier: email, limit: 5, windowMs: 60_000 }`, to blunt spam without new infra. - Look up an existing row via the new index; if found, return `{ alreadyJoined: true }` instead of inserting a duplicate; otherwise insert and return `{ alreadyJoined: false }`. - No auth required — this must work for signed-out visitors on a marketing page. **Frontend wiring:** - Use `useConvexClient()` (`src/utils/convex-context.tsx`) exactly as `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx` does, plus `api.waitlist.join` from `convex/_generated/api`. - Per-card local state (`useSignal`) for the email input value and a submit status (`idle | submitting | joined | error`) so both cards work independently. - On success (`joined` or `alreadyJoined`), swap the form for a short confirmation line ("You're on the list — we'll email you."). ### 4. Expand "why desktop over browser" copy - Replace/expand the single intro paragraph under "Desktop app" with a short benefits list grounded in what's actually true in the codebase (`desktop/main.ts`, `electrobun.config.ts`): - Distraction-free native window — no browser tabs/address bar around your writing. - Deep-link ATProto sign-in via the registered `twyne://` URL scheme (smoother OAuth callback than a browser redirect). - Its own dock/taskbar icon and app-switcher entry, separate from your browser. - Same account, sync, and hosted AI as the web — nothing to reconfigure switching between them. - Keep the existing "Your data travels with you" section as-is (it's about local-first/export, a distinct point). ## Files touched - `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx` — detection logic, new styles via `useStylesScoped$`, new mobile waitlist section, expanded benefits copy, updated `toc`. - `convex/schema.ts` — add `waitlist` table + index. - `convex/waitlist.ts` — new `join` mutation. ## Verification - Run Convex dev (schema push) and the app dev server; open `/downloads/` in Chrome via the claude-in-chrome tool. - Confirm SSR/initial render shows the plain desktop grid with no flash, then after hydration the browser's OS gets stamped "Recommended" and the intro line fills in. - Spot-check on the current Linux host that the Linux card gets recommended (real detection, no spoofing needed for a sanity check). - Submit an email on the iOS/Android waitlist card, confirm it succeeds and shows the confirmation line; submit the same email again and confirm it's treated as already-joined (no duplicate row, no error) — check via the Convex dashboard/CLI that only one row exists. - Submit an invalid email and confirm a client-side/server-side validation error surfaces instead of a silent failure. - Check responsive layout at mobile width (existing `.dl-grid` breakpoint at 720px) still holds with the added section.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. - entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

content.text:
It's not a curve issue — the curve leaves anything ≤50 raw untouched, so F is mathematically reachable. The reason it's hard to *hit* in practice is upstream: `combineJudgesAndStatic()` in `src/utils/rubric.ts:406-428` blends judges 70/30 with the static-feature score (length, structure, pacing, etc.), and that static component tends to score moderately even for bad writing as long as it's grammatically competent and reasonably formatted — it's measuring mechanics, not judgment about quality. So even if all five judges tank a draft, the static 30% floats the blend up out of F range unless judges are *unanimously* scoring below 4 (which also triggers the `lowPenalty`, clamped so `judgeMean` never drops below 1).

The lever that actually controls this: shift weight toward judges (e.g. `JUDGE_WEIGHT`/`STATIC_WEIGHT` from 0.7/0.3 to something like 0.85/0.15), and/or drop the `clamp(1, 10, ...)` floor on `judgeMean` to `clamp(0, 10, ...)` so genuinely bad judge consensus isn't propped up. Tradeoff: this makes static mechanics matter less overall, so a well-structured-but-shallow draft would grade closer to how the judges actually feel about it rather than getting cushioned.

Want me to make that change?

The static features (length/structure/pacing/etc.) are all mechanical — they can't judge whether the *argument* is any good, so adding another rule-based metric won't fix the "hard to get an F" problem; it'd just be more mechanics propping up the score. What would actually move the needle is a **worst-judge (min score) component**, weighted alongside the mean — right now one scathing persona gets diluted into an average of five. Blending in `minJudgeScore` (e.g. `judgeMean * 0.45 + minJudge * 0.35 + staticTotal * 0.20`) means a single "this doesn't work" verdict can drag the grade down hard, which also fits Twyne's "brutal room" framing better than an averaged consensus.

Tradeoff: a single contrarian or miscalibrated judge now has outsized influence on the grade, so it raises variance — one persona with a bad day can tank an otherwise decent draft.

# Downloads page: OS detection, mobile "coming soon", fun interactions, benefits copy ## Context `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx` already has a solid downloads page: a 3-card desktop grid (macOS/Windows/Linux) linking to `/download/[platform]` (a GitHub-releases redirect endpoint), a "web/PWA" callout, a data-portability checklist, and release notes. It's missing what the user asked for: 1. Detecting the visitor's OS and surfacing the right download instead of making them scan three identical cards. 2. A visible "coming soon" section for mobile apps (iOS/Android) — currently absent entirely. 3. More personality/delight in the interactions — currently static. 4. A clearer, more persuasive explanation of *why* someone would want the desktop app over just using the browser — currently one paragraph + a generic checklist that's really about local-first data, not about desktop-vs-browser. This touches the frontend (`src/routes/downloads/index.tsx`) plus a small new Convex backend piece: the user confirmed the mobile "coming soon" section should have a real waitlist (email capture), not just a mailto link — there's no existing waitlist mechanism in the codebase, so this adds one. ## Approach All changes are in `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx`. ### 1. OS detection (client-only, progressive enhancement) - Add a `useSignal<"macos" | "windows" | "linux" | null>(null)` for the detected platform. - Add a `useVisibleTask$` that runs once on the client, parsing `navigator.userAgentData?.platform` (modern Chromium) with fallback to `navigator.userAgent`/`navigator.platform` string sniffing (mac/win/linux tokens) — same alias set already defined server-side in `download/[platform]/index.ts` (`PLATFORM_ALIASES`), just mirrored client-side since we can't import a server route module into a browser task. - SSR renders the plain 3-card grid (no layout shift, no flash of wrong content); once hydrated and detected, the matching card gets a highlighted state — no reordering of the DOM (avoids layout jank), just a visual treatment change. ### 2. Highlight the detected platform card - Reuse the existing `/approval-stamp.svg` + `.stamp-tilt` rubber-stamp motif already used on the landing page (`landing-broadsheet.tsx`, `landing-quarterly.tsx`) for a "Recommended" stamp on the detected card — this keeps the fun/playful bit on-brand with the editorial/broadsheet aesthetic rather than introducing a generic UI badge. - Add a small line above the grid that fills in once detection completes, e.g. "Looks like you're on **macOS**." with a typewriter-style fade-in (matches the site's `--font-typewriter` motif), staying blank/generic during SSR. ### 3. Mobile "coming soon" section with a real waitlist - New `

Mobile apps

` section (added to the `toc` array too) with two cards (iOS, Android) styled like the desktop cards but visually "stamped" as coming soon (reuse the same stamp asset, rotated the other way via `.stamp-tilt-r`, with text "Coming soon" instead of "Recommended"). - Each card has an inline email input + "Notify me" button (no disabled/fake download link — this is the real CTA for mobile). **Backend (new):** - `convex/schema.ts` — add a `waitlist` table: `{ email: string, platform: v.union(v.literal("ios"), v.literal("android")), createdAt: number }`, indexed `by_email_platform` on `["email", "platform"]` for dedupe lookups. - `convex/waitlist.ts` — new file, one public mutation `join({ email, platform })`: - Validate `email` is a plausible address (simple regex — same bar as other client-facing forms in this codebase; no external verification service). - Rate-limit via the existing `consumeRateLimit` helper (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts`, same helper used in `convex/research.ts`), e.g. `{ action: "waitlist:join", identifier: email, limit: 5, windowMs: 60_000 }`, to blunt spam without new infra. - Look up an existing row via the new index; if found, return `{ alreadyJoined: true }` instead of inserting a duplicate; otherwise insert and return `{ alreadyJoined: false }`. - No auth required — this must work for signed-out visitors on a marketing page. **Frontend wiring:** - Use `useConvexClient()` (`src/utils/convex-context.tsx`) exactly as `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx` does, plus `api.waitlist.join` from `convex/_generated/api`. - Per-card local state (`useSignal`) for the email input value and a submit status (`idle | submitting | joined | error`) so both cards work independently. - On success (`joined` or `alreadyJoined`), swap the form for a short confirmation line ("You're on the list — we'll email you."). ### 4. Expand "why desktop over browser" copy - Replace/expand the single intro paragraph under "Desktop app" with a short benefits list grounded in what's actually true in the codebase (`desktop/main.ts`, `electrobun.config.ts`): - Distraction-free native window — no browser tabs/address bar around your writing. - Deep-link ATProto sign-in via the registered `twyne://` URL scheme (smoother OAuth callback than a browser redirect). - Its own dock/taskbar icon and app-switcher entry, separate from your browser. - Same account, sync, and hosted AI as the web — nothing to reconfigure switching between them. - Keep the existing "Your data travels with you" section as-is (it's about local-first/export, a distinct point). ## Files touched - `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx` — detection logic, new styles via `useStylesScoped$`, new mobile waitlist section, expanded benefits copy, updated `toc`. - `convex/schema.ts` — add `waitlist` table + index. - `convex/waitlist.ts` — new `join` mutation. ## Verification - Run Convex dev (schema push) and the app dev server; open `/downloads/` in Chrome via the claude-in-chrome tool. - Confirm SSR/initial render shows the plain desktop grid with no flash, then after hydration the browser's OS gets stamped "Recommended" and the intro line fills in. - Spot-check on the current Linux host that the Linux card gets recommended (real detection, no spoofing needed for a sanity check). - Submit an email on the iOS/Android waitlist card, confirm it succeeds and shows the confirmation line; submit the same email again and confirm it's treated as already-joined (no duplicate row, no error) — check via the Convex dashboard/CLI that only one row exists. - Submit an invalid email and confirm a client-side/server-side validation error surfaces instead of a silent failure. - Check responsive layout at mobile width (existing `.dl-grid` breakpoint at 720px) still holds with the added section.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

content.text:
Confirmed public, unauthenticated. Now I have everything needed.

## Findings

**1. "Dossier"** = the project brief from the onboarding interview (`src/routes/dossier/create/`, `src/routes/dossier/refine/`). It's created locally via `createProjectBrief`/`saveProjectBrief` (IndexedDB first), but is also synced server-side to Convex: table `briefs` (`convex/schema.ts`): `{ userId: string, brief: v.any(), updatedAt: number }`, with `convex/sync.ts` exposing `getBrief`/`putBrief`. It's a **single row per user, "latest wins"** — no history of multiple dossiers/projects and no per-day granularity.

**2. "Folio"** = a writing project/piece, typed in `src/types/index.ts`. Originally IndexedDB-only (`src/utils/idb.ts`: `loadFoliosFromIdb`/`saveFoliosToIdb`/`folioContent` store for HTML body), but now also mirrored to Convex via `convex/sync.ts`: table `folios` = `{ userId, folios: v.array(v.any()), updatedAt }` (whole list as one blob, not one row per folio) and `folioContent` = `{ userId, folioId, html, updatedAt }` indexed by `by_userId_folioId`. So folio existence/count is synced, but only as a single denormalized array with **one `updatedAt` for the whole list**, not per-folio creation timestamps — you'd need to inspect the `folios` array's own item shape (in `src/types/index.ts`) for any internal `createdAt` per folio.

**3. Profile pages**: Two distinct routes exist.
- `src/routes/[handle]/index.tsx` — **public**, unauthenticated, shows handle/displayName/bio/avatar + published pieces list. Wrong place for private stats.
- `src/routes/settings/index.tsx` — **private, authed** account page (AI provider config, writer prefs, apparatus settings, account deletion). This is the natural home for a usage/stats dashboard.

**4. Convex tables with timestamps** (all are "one row per user, latest wins" style, not append-only logs): `briefs`, `folios`, `folioContent`, `customPersonas`, `rubricResults`, `roomSettings`, `bibliographies` each have a single `updatedAt`. Append-only-ish tables that do have per-event timestamps: `personaNotes` (`createdAt` per note), `personaReplies` (`createdAt`), `suggestions` (`createdAt`), `userComments`/`userCommentReplies` (`createdAt`), `published` (`publishedAt`/`updatedAt`), `webhookEvents`, `rateBuckets` (windowed, not useful).

**5. Analytics**: `convex/posthog.ts` sends AI-generation events (feature/provider/model/latency) to PostHog server-side — external, not queryable back from Convex for a heatmap. `convex/arizeTracing.ts` similarly instruments LLM spans to Arize. Neither is a first-party Convex table you can query per-day per-user.

**6. Rubric runs**: `rubricResults` table stores only the **latest** result per user (`updatedAt` overwritten each run) — no history, so it can't alone build a multi-day heatmap without schema changes.

**Best heatmap proxy today**: `personaNotes.createdAt`, `personaReplies.createdAt`, `suggestions.createdAt`, and `userComments.createdAt`/`userCommentReplies.createdAt` are the only genuinely append-only, per-user, timestamped Convex records — these could be aggregated by day as an activity proxy. Everything else (briefs, folios, rubric, room settings) only exposes a single `updatedAt`, so true "days writing" would require either a new append-only events table or bucketing the existing note/reply/comment/suggestion timestamps by day.

**Min-judge weighting** (fully propagated): `judgeMean` 45% + harshest-`minJudge` 35% + `staticTotal` 20%, threaded through `rubric.ts` → `ai-client.ts` → `agentPrompts.ts` → `agents.ts` → `rubric-panel.tsx` payload. Tests/typecheck/lint all clean.

- **Bullshit Resistance** — currently regex-based (filler/vague-word lists, universal-claim detection). Misses sophisticated bullshit and can false-positive on legitimate emphatic language.

Both are the same shape of problem as sufficiency was. Want me to convert either (or both) to LLM judges the same way, or leave them as static/mechanical checks?

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: - **(Completed)** Propagate the previously-authorized "min judge" rubric scoring change (`minJudge` = harshest judge's raw score, blended in at 35% alongside judgeMean 45% and staticTotal 20%) through the full call chain: `src/utils/rubric.ts`, `src/utils/ai-client.ts`, `convex/agentPrompts.ts`, `convex/agents.ts`, `src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx`, and test fixtures. Verified via tsc/eslint/tests. - **(Completed)** "update the card explaining the grades" — rewrote the "Why a 'good' draft is still a C" explainer paragraph in `src/routes/rubric/index.tsx` to describe the new 45/35/20 weighting instead of the old 70/30 split. - **(Completed, then revised per feedback)** "i want to also add a category that judges if the given text has the appropriate amount of content to justifiably reach the thesis or goal" — added a new "Sufficiency & Development" `RubricCriterion`. Initially implemented as a keyword-overlap heuristic; user explicitly rejected this as "not really good at all way too inflexible," so it was converted to a dedicated LLM judge (`convex/agents.ts: judgeSufficiency` action) with the heuristic demoted to an offline/fallback-only path. - **(User declined further scope)** I proposed converting two more mechanical criteria — "Evidence & Support" (citation-count based) and "Bullshit Resistance" (regex-based) — to LLM judges as well, following the same pattern. User explicitly said **"not those gaps but work on the dashboard"** — declining this additional work and redirecting to the next task. - **(Current, in progress)** "add a page that is about usage i want dashboards and other metrics on writing and results that you have the amount of dossiers how often you have been wrritiing i would like the github days writing graph as well i want all these for the person and should be in their prile" — build a usage/stats dashboard (as a page, in the user's private profile/account area) showing: number of dossiers, writing frequency metrics, and a GitHub-style "days writing" contribution graph/heatmap. This is Task #8 in the tracked task list, currently being planned (in plan mode, no code written yet). 2. Key Technical Concepts: - Qwik framework: `component , `useStore`, `useVisibleTask , `useStylesScoped , `$()` QRLs, Qwik City `Link`, file-based routing. - Convex: `mutation`/`query`/`action`, `v.*` validators, `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` for auth (never accept `userId` as an argument — enforced convention per `convex/sync.ts`'s own doc comment and Convex AI guidelines), indexes (`by_userId`, `by_userId_folioId`, etc.), `consumeRateLimit`/`RATE_LIMITS` helper. - Rubric scoring pipeline: `scoreStaticFeatures` (mechanical/rule-based features) vs. LLM "judges" (`JudgeResult[]`, persona-voiced 0-10 scores) vs. `combineJudgesAndStatic()` (blends `judgeMean`(45%) + `minJudge`(35%, harshest judge) + `staticTotal`(20%) into `combinedTen`, then `brutalCurve()` maps to 0-100, then `letterGrade()`). - **New architectural pattern established this session**: for any rubric dimension requiring semantic/content judgment (not purely mechanical/countable), the correct pattern is a dedicated LLM judge action (mirroring `judgeDraft`'s shape: single LLM call with JSON `{score, rationale}` output via `parseJudgeOutput`), with a cheap heuristic function retained ONLY as an offline/signed-out/no-provider fallback — never as the primary signal. This was an explicit user correction and should generalize to any future rubric-criterion work. - Convex sync layer (`convex/sync.ts`): per-table `getX` (read latest, single row per user via `by_userId` index) / `putX` (upsert) pattern for `briefs`, `folios` (whole array as one document), `folioContent` (per-folio HTML, keyed `by_userId_folioId`), `customPersonas`, `personaNotes`, `personaReplies`, `rubricResults`, `bibliographies`. Most tables are "latest wins" (single `updatedAt`), NOT append-only logs — this is the central architectural constraint for the dashboard task. - `Folio` type (`src/types/index.ts:254-266`) DOES carry its own `createdAt`/`updatedAt` per-piece, even though the Convex `folios` table stores the whole list as one blob document (`{ userId, folios: v.array(v.any()), updatedAt }`) — so per-folio timestamps exist but aren't natively queryable/indexed server-side; they'd need to be unpacked from the array. - Genuinely append-only, per-user, per-event-timestamped Convex tables identified: `personaNotes.createdAt`, `personaReplies.createdAt`, `suggestions.createdAt`, `userComments.createdAt`, `userCommentReplies.createdAt`, `published.publishedAt`/`updatedAt`. - Two private/authed vs public route distinction: `src/routes/settings/index.tsx` (private, authed, account/settings — natural home for a usage dashboard) vs. `src/routes/[handle]/index.tsx` (public profile page, unauthenticated, shows only handle/bio/avatar/published pieces). - GitHub-style "days writing" contribution graph: a calendar heatmap UI concept the user wants, requiring genuine per-day activity data — which the current schema does NOT cleanly support without either a new append-only table or approximating from existing per-event tables/folio array timestamps. 3. # Downloads page: OS detection, mobile "coming soon", fun interactions, benefits copy ## Context `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx` already has a solid downloads page: a 3-card desktop grid (macOS/Windows/Linux) linking to `/download/[platform]` (a GitHub-releases redirect endpoint), a "web/PWA" callout, a data-portability checklist, and release notes. It's missing what the user asked for: 1. Detecting the visitor's OS and surfacing the right download instead of making them scan three identical cards. 2. A visible "coming soon" section for mobile apps (iOS/Android) — currently absent entirely. 3. More personality/delight in the interactions — currently static. 4. A clearer, more persuasive explanation of *why* someone would want the desktop app over just using the browser — currently one paragraph + a generic checklist that's really about local-first data, not about desktop-vs-browser. This touches the frontend (`src/routes/downloads/index.tsx`) plus a small new Convex backend piece: the user confirmed the mobile "coming soon" section should have a real waitlist (email capture), not just a mailto link — there's no existing waitlist mechanism in the codebase, so this adds one. ## Approach All changes are in `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx`. ### 1. OS detection (client-only, progressive enhancement) - Add a `useSignal<"macos" | "windows" | "linux" | null>(null)` for the detected platform. - Add a `useVisibleTask$` that runs once on the client, parsing `navigator.userAgentData?.platform` (modern Chromium) with fallback to `navigator.userAgent`/`navigator.platform` string sniffing (mac/win/linux tokens) — same alias set already defined server-side in `download/[platform]/index.ts` (`PLATFORM_ALIASES`), just mirrored client-side since we can't import a server route module into a browser task. - SSR renders the plain 3-card grid (no layout shift, no flash of wrong content); once hydrated and detected, the matching card gets a highlighted state — no reordering of the DOM (avoids layout jank), just a visual treatment change. ### 2. Highlight the detected platform card - Reuse the existing `/approval-stamp.svg` + `.stamp-tilt` rubber-stamp motif already used on the landing page (`landing-broadsheet.tsx`, `landing-quarterly.tsx`) for a "Recommended" stamp on the detected card — this keeps the fun/playful bit on-brand with the editorial/broadsheet aesthetic rather than introducing a generic UI badge. - Add a small line above the grid that fills in once detection completes, e.g. "Looks like you're on **macOS**." with a typewriter-style fade-in (matches the site's `--font-typewriter` motif), staying blank/generic during SSR. ### 3. Mobile "coming soon" section with a real waitlist - New `

Mobile apps

` section (added to the `toc` array too) with two cards (iOS, Android) styled like the desktop cards but visually "stamped" as coming soon (reuse the same stamp asset, rotated the other way via `.stamp-tilt-r`, with text "Coming soon" instead of "Recommended"). - Each card has an inline email input + "Notify me" button (no disabled/fake download link — this is the real CTA for mobile). **Backend (new):** - `convex/schema.ts` — add a `waitlist` table: `{ email: string, platform: v.union(v.literal("ios"), v.literal("android")), createdAt: number }`, indexed `by_email_platform` on `["email", "platform"]` for dedupe lookups. - `convex/waitlist.ts` — new file, one public mutation `join({ email, platform })`: - Validate `email` is a plausible address (simple regex — same bar as other client-facing forms in this codebase; no external verification service). - Rate-limit via the existing `consumeRateLimit` helper (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts`, same helper used in `convex/research.ts`), e.g. `{ action: "waitlist:join", identifier: email, limit: 5, windowMs: 60_000 }`, to blunt spam without new infra. - Look up an existing row via the new index; if found, return `{ alreadyJoined: true }` instead of inserting a duplicate; otherwise insert and return `{ alreadyJoined: false }`. - No auth required — this must work for signed-out visitors on a marketing page. **Frontend wiring:** - Use `useConvexClient()` (`src/utils/convex-context.tsx`) exactly as `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx` does, plus `api.waitlist.join` from `convex/_generated/api`. - Per-card local state (`useSignal`) for the email input value and a submit status (`idle | submitting | joined | error`) so both cards work independently. - On success (`joined` or `alreadyJoined`), swap the form for a short confirmation line ("You're on the list — we'll email you."). ### 4. Expand "why desktop over browser" copy - Replace/expand the single intro paragraph under "Desktop app" with a short benefits list grounded in what's actually true in the codebase (`desktop/main.ts`, `electrobun.config.ts`): - Distraction-free native window — no browser tabs/address bar around your writing. - Deep-link ATProto sign-in via the registered `twyne://` URL scheme (smoother OAuth callback than a browser redirect). - Its own dock/taskbar icon and app-switcher entry, separate from your browser. - Same account, sync, and hosted AI as the web — nothing to reconfigure switching between them. - Keep the existing "Your data travels with you" section as-is (it's about local-first/export, a distinct point). ## Files touched - `src/routes/downloads/index.tsx` — detection logic, new styles via `useStylesScoped$`, new mobile waitlist section, expanded benefits copy, updated `toc`. - `convex/schema.ts` — add `waitlist` table + index. - `convex/waitlist.ts` — new `join` mutation. ## Verification - Run Convex dev (schema push) and the app dev server; open `/downloads/` in Chrome via the claude-in-chrome tool. - Confirm SSR/initial render shows the plain desktop grid with no flash, then after hydration the browser's OS gets stamped "Recommended" and the intro line fills in. - Spot-check on the current Linux host that the Linux card gets recommended (real detection, no spoofing needed for a sanity check). - Submit an email on the iOS/Android waitlist card, confirm it succeeds and shows the confirmation line; submit the same email again and confirm it's treated as already-joined (no duplicate row, no error) — check via the Convex dashboard/CLI that only one row exists. - Submit an invalid email and confirm a client-side/server-side validation error surfaces instead of a silent failure. - Check responsive layout at mobile width (existing `.dl-grid` breakpoint at 720px) still holds with the added section.

/**
 * Writer handles — first-class public identity.
 *
 * A handle is a writer's addressable name on Twyne: it appears in share URLs
 * (`/<handle>/<slug>`), profile pages (`/<handle>`), and is the only
 * user-facing identifier surfaced publicly. Claimed once a user signs in,
 * the handle is denormalized onto `published.ownerHandle` at publish time so
 * the reader route never needs a second hop.
 *
 * Rules:

 *     a hyphen, can't have two hyphens in a row.
 *   • Not all-numeric (avoids slug collisions and `_id` confusion).
 *   • Reserved words (existing top-level routes: `blog`, `editor`, etc.)
 *     are rejected so a handle can never shadow a Twyne route.
 *   • Uniqueness is enforced at write time via the `by_handle` index.
 *
 * Auth follows the Convex guideline: every mutation reads identity from

# Public writing dashboard: dossier count, frequency, GitHub-style activity graph

## Context

The user wants a stats/usage dashboard about their writing — how many folios ("dossiers") they have, how often they write, and a GitHub-style day-by-day contribution heatmap — surfaced publicly on their author profile (`/<handle>`), matching how GitHub's contribution graph works: public, visible to anyone, no separate private view needed. (Confirmed via AskUserQuestion: public on profile, not a private Settings-only view.)

"Amount of dossiers" will use folio count for now — the user realized project briefs are currently one-per-account, not one-per-folio as they'd like, but explicitly deferred that restructuring as separate follow-up work. This dashboard just counts folios (the only real multi-item collection today, same thing the Library page already calls "folios").

The hard part: there is no existing per-day activity signal in the schema. Every relevant table (`briefs`, `folios`, `folioContent`) is "latest wins" — one row per user, overwritten on every save. `Folio.createdAt`/`updatedAt` exist per-piece but live inside one blob array (`folios.folios: v.array(v.any())`), so at most you'd learn the day each folio was *last* touched, not every day it was worked on. A real GitHub-style graph needs a genuine append-only per-day record, so this plan adds one.

## Approach

### 1. New schema table: `writingActivity` (`convex/schema.ts`)

```ts
writingActivity: defineTable({
  userId: v.string(),
  day: v.string(),      // "YYYY-MM-DD", UTC
  count: v.number(),    // rough intensity signal, like GitHub's commit count
  updatedAt: v.number(),
})
  .index("by_userId_day", ["userId", "day"])
  .index("by_userId", ["userId"]),
```

One row per user per day. `count` increments each time activity is recorded that day (throttled client-side, see below) — gives the heatmap gradient variation instead of flat on/off.

### 2. New Convex file: `convex/writingActivity.ts`

Follows the `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` convention (no `userId` args) used throughout, e.g. `convex/profiles.ts`.

- `recordActivity` — **mutation**, auth required, no args. Computes today's UTC day string, upserts the `(userId, day)` row via `by_userId_day` (increment `count`, bump `updatedAt`, insert if missing). Rate-limited via the existing `consumeRateLimit`/`RATE_LIMITS` helper (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts`) with a generous per-minute cap (e.g. 10/min) — cheap insurance, not a real constraint given client-side throttling.
- `getMyActivity` — **query**, auth required. Returns the last ~371 days of `{day, count}` for the signed-in user (`by_userId` index, filter/sort by day), plus folio count (via existing `getFolios`-style lookup on the `folios` table). Not strictly needed for the public-only scope, but trivial to include and useful if a private view is ever added later — skip if it adds not-asked-for surface area; the public query below is the one actually wired up.
- `getPublicActivity` — **query** (no auth), args `{ handle: string }`. Mirrors `profiles.ts`'s `getProfile` handle lookup (`handles` table `by_handle` index) to resolve `userId`, returns `null` if handle unknown. Otherwise returns `{ days: {day, count}[], folioCount: number }` — `days` from `writingActivity` via `by_userId`, `folioCount` from reading the user's `folios` row (`folios.folios.length`, defaulting to 0 if no row). This is the data source for the public profile page.

### 3. Wire `recordActivity` into the editor's existing autosave path

`src/utils/convex-sync.ts:228` (`markDirty()`) already debounces a `pushLocalSnapshot()` call whenever the draft changes — this is the natural hook. Add a client-side throttle (module-level `lastRecordedAt` timestamp, e.g. skip if <2 min since last call) inside `markDirty()` or a sibling function called alongside it, so a writing session generates a handful of `recordActivity` calls (giving `count` some gradient) without spamming the mutation on every keystroke-debounce tick.

### 4. Public profile page: new "Writing" section (`src/routes/[handle]/index.tsx`)

- Call `api.writingActivity.getPublicActivity({ handle })` alongside the existing profile/published-posts data fetch (same `useVisibleTask$` + `useConvexClient()` pattern already in this file).
- Render a new section (after the bio header, before the posts list) with:
  - Folio count, phrased in the site's editorial voice (e.g. "N pieces on the desk").
  – A frequency line derived client-side from `days` (e.g. "wrote on N of the last 30 days").
  - A GitHub-style heatmap: new small component `src/components/profile/writing-heatmap.tsx` — grid of week-columns × 7 day-rows, square color intensity bucketed from `count` (0/low/med/high/very-high, 5 shades using existing CSS vars like `--color-paper-3`/`--color-vermilion` for on-brand styling rather than GitHub's green), simple legend ("Less → More"). No auth needed since this is public data for the handle in the URL.
- If a handle has no `writingActivity` rows yet (new/inactive writer), render an empty-state grid (all-zero) rather than hiding the section — consistent with how the rest of the page already handles a writer with zero posts.

### Files touched
- `convex/schema.ts` — add `writingActivity` table + two indexes.
- `convex/writingActivity.ts` — new file: `recordActivity` mutation, `getPublicActivity` query (drop `getMyActivity` if it turns out unused — start without it, add only if a private view is requested later).
- `src/utils/convex-sync.ts` — throttled `recordActivity` call wired alongside `markDirty()`.
- `src/routes/[handle]/index.tsx` — new "Writing" section: folio count, frequency line, heatmap.
- `src/components/profile/writing-heatmap.tsx` — new small presentational component.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and `npx eslint` clean.
- Run Convex dev to push the schema change; confirm `writingActivity` table appears.
- In the browser (claude-in-chrome): sign in, write/edit a draft in the editor, confirm (via Convex dashboard or a temporary log) that `recordActivity` fires and a `writingActivity` row appears/increments for today.
- Visit `/<handle>` for that account and confirm the new Writing section renders: folio count matches Library, heatmap shows today's square lit up, frequency line is sane.
- Visit `/<handle>` for a handle with no activity yet and confirm the empty-state grid renders without errors.

input.prompt:
I'm investigating the Twyne codebase (Qwik frontend + Convex backend) at /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne, to plan restructuring "dossiers" (project briefs) from one-per-account to one-per-folio.

Background: `ProjectBrief` is the onboarding interview result (goal, audience, constraints etc. — an interview the user does before writing) referred to in the UI as a "dossier". Currently:
- `convex/schema.ts` has a `briefs` table: `{ userId: string, brief: v.any(), updatedAt: number }` indexed only `by_userId` — ONE brief per user, no folio association.
- `convex/sync.ts` has `getBrief`/`putBrief` — single-row-per-user query/mutation (see lines ~36-64).
- `folios` table stores `{ userId, folios: v.array(v.any()), updatedAt }` — the WHOLE list of folios (pieces/drafts) as one blob array, each folio object having its own `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` etc. (see `src/types/index.ts` Folio interface).
- There's a separate `folioContent` table, keyed `by_userId_folioId`, storing just the HTML body per folio — this IS already per-folio (good precedent pattern to imitate).

I need a THOROUGH report (this is "very thorough" breadth) covering:

1. **Everywhere `ProjectBrief` / "brief" / "dossier" is read or written**, across both `convex/*.ts` and `src/**/*.tsx`/`.ts`. I need concrete file:line references. Specifically:
   - Onboarding/interview flow that creates a brief (likely `src/routes/onboarding/...` or similar) — where does the interview get kicked off, and is it tied to creating a NEW folio, or independent of folios entirely?
   - Where does the editor (`src/routes/editor/index.tsx`) read the current brief to show goal/audience context, and where does it pass `brief` into AI calls (rubric judges, room-of-editors personas, agents.ts actions)?
   - `src/utils/convex-sync.ts` — how `getBrief`/`putBrief` are called (pushLocalSnapshot, handleUserChanged, pullAll/pushAll in sync.ts) and whether brief syncing is coupled to folio syncing already or fully separate.
   - Any local IndexedDB-side storage of the brief (`src/utils/idb.ts` or `lix.ts`) — is there a `BRIEF_PATH` or similar single-brief-per-account convention there too?
   - Any UI component that lets the user switch between folios (a "Library" page/folio switcher) — does switching folios currently swap which brief is shown, or is the brief totally global regardless of active folio?

2. **The `Folio` type shape** (`src/types/index.ts`) — exact fields, especially whether it already has any brief-related field (e.g. `briefId`, `goal`, embedded brief data) or if brief and folio are entirely disconnected today.

3. **How many places assume "the brief" is a singleton** — e.g. any global signal/store like `useStore` holding one `ProjectBrief | null` for the whole app, versus something already keyed by active folio id.

4. **The multi-folio switching UX** — how does `activeFolioId` work (`loadActiveFolioIdFromIdb` mentioned in convex-sync.ts) and where is it set/read, since the per-folio brief will need to be swapped in/out whenever the active folio changes, mirroring how `folioContent` already does per-folio HTML swapping.

Report back with concrete file:line citations for all of the above, organized by these 4 numbered sections. Don't propose a solution — just report the current architecture facts I need to design against. Keep the report information-dense; a partial code snippet for key call sites is more useful than prose description.

options.label: Optional, add later (Recommended)

options.description: Creating a folio always kicks off the onboarding interview first, before the writer can start the piece. Bigger UX change to the folio-creation flow.

options.label: Attach to their active folio (Recommended)
options.description: The one existing brief becomes the dossier for whichever folio is currently active/most recent. Other folios start dossier-less, same as new ones.

options.label: Copy to every existing folio
options.description: The existing brief is duplicated as the starting dossier for every folio the user already has, so nothing looks newly "missing" after the migration.

options.description: Notes and outlines can also carry their own dossier/goal, treated uniformly with drafts.

# Dossier per folio (not per account)

## Context

The project brief ("dossier" — the onboarding interview: goal, audience, tone, constraints) is currently a single global object per account: one `briefs` row per `userId` server-side, one fixed `localStorage`/Lix path client-side. Folios (individual pieces/drafts) are already a real multi-item collection with their own per-folio content storage (`folioContent` table, `folio-content` IDB store). The user wants each folio to carry its own dossier, since a writer's goal/audience/tone genuinely differs piece to piece.

Confirmed scope (via AskUserQuestion):
- Dossier stays **optional per folio** — new folios created from the editor start dossier-less (`brief: null`), same UX as an empty dossier today; the writer can open the interview for that folio whenever they want.
- Existing users' one legacy global brief **migrates to whichever folio is currently active** on first load after this ships; other existing folios start dossier-less.
- **All** folio types (draft/notes/outline) can carry a dossier, not just drafts — uniform treatment, no type-based branching.

The good news: the plumbing for "per-folio state that swaps when the active folio changes" already exists and is exercised today for folio content (`loadFolioContentFromIdb`/`saveFolioContentToIdb`, swapped into `store.editorSeed` on every folio switch in `src/routes/editor/index.tsx`). There's even a **half-built, currently-dead** per-folio brief IDB store already in `src/utils/idb.ts` (`loadBriefFromIdb(folioId)` / `saveBriefToIdb(folioId, brief)`, object store keyed `folioId`) — this plan resurrects and wires that up rather than inventing new storage.

## Approach

### 1. Schema (`convex/schema.ts`)
Add `folioId: v.optional(v.string())` to the `briefs` table, plus a `by_userId_folioId` index (mirroring `folioContent`'s `by_userId_folioId`). Keep the field optional so existing rows (which predate this change) don't fail schema validation — they simply become orphaned/unreachable through the new index, which is fine: the actual legacy-brief continuity for existing users comes from a **client-side** migration (see §6), not from re-reading these old server rows.

### 2. Server sync functions (`convex/sync.ts`)
Rework `getBrief`/`putBrief` to be folio-scoped, mirroring `getFolioContent`/`putFolioContent` exactly:
- `getBrief({ folioId })` — query by `by_userId_folioId`.
- `putBrief({ folioId, brief })` — upsert by the same index.
- Add `listBriefs()` (no args) — returns all of the signed-in user's briefs, mirroring `listFolioContent`. Used by `pullAll`.
- `pushAll`/`pullAll` — replace the flat `brief`/`briefUpdatedAt` fields with a `briefs: { folioId, brief, updatedAt }[]` array, exactly parallel to how `folioContent` is already handled in both functions.

### 3. Client storage (`src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`)
- `loadProjectBrief(folioId: string)` — delegate to `loadBriefFromIdb(folioId)` (resurrecting the dead code in `idb.ts`), keep the existing shape-normalization logic (`normalizeInterviewAnswers`, defaults for `attachments`/`completedAt`/`updatedAt`).
- `saveProjectBrief(folioId: string, brief: ProjectBrief)` — delegate to `saveBriefToIdb(folioId, brief)`, then call `markSyncDirty()` directly (same effect as today, just without the Lix round-trip).
- Drop the `localStorage` (`BRIEF_STORAGE_KEY`) write and the Lix (`BRIEF_PATH`, `writeFileAsJson`) write — the per-folio IDB store is now the source of truth, consistent with how folio content already works (it never used Lix either). Keep `BRIEF_STORAGE_KEY`/`localStorage.getItem` readable one more time, read-only, purely for the one-time legacy migration in §6.

### 4. Sync orchestration (`src/utils/convex-sync.ts`)
- `LocalSnapshot.brief` → `LocalSnapshot.briefs: { folioId: string; brief: ProjectBrief }[]`, built in `buildLocalSnapshot` by looping the same folio-id `Set` already assembled for `folioContent` (lines ~286-295) and calling `loadBriefFromIdb(id)` per id, skipping nulls.
- `pushLocalSnapshot` — send `briefs: snap.briefs` to `api.sync.pushAll` instead of the flat field.
- `mergeFromRemote` — loop `remote.briefs`, per-folioId newer-wins compare against the local `loadBriefFromIdb(folioId)`, write via `saveBriefToIdb(folioId, brief)` — same shape as the existing `folioContent` loop right next to it.
- `handleUserChanged`'s `hasRemoteData` check — swap `remote.brief !== null` for `remote.briefs.length > 0`.

### 5. Editor (`src/routes/editor/index.tsx`)
- Hydration block (~lines 175-212): after `activeFolioId` is resolved, set `store.brief = await loadProjectBrief(activeFolioId)`.
- All three folio-switch call sites (existing-folio click ~553-566, new folio via Enter ~595-620, new folio via the Create button ~624-646) — alongside the existing `editorSeed`/`activeFolioId` updates, also set `store.brief = await loadProjectBrief(folio.id)` (null for a brand-new folio) and re-call `startBackgroundResearch({ client, brief: store.brief, folioId: folio.id })`. This last part is a small bonus fix: `background-research.ts` currently caches `brief`/`folioId` in module-level variables set once at mount and never refreshed on folio switch (confirmed via exploration) — re-calling it here fixes that staleness as a natural side effect of making brief folio-aware.
- `onStartInterview$` handler (~line 529, passed to `ProjectBriefCard`) — currently always navigates to `/dossier/refine/`, which silently no-ops when there's no brief to refine. Change to branch: `nav(store.brief ? "/dossier/refine/" : "/dossier/create/")`. This bug is latent today (onboarding's old gate guaranteed a brief always existed by the time you reached the editor) but becomes reachable now that folios can be dossier-less.

### 6. First-run onboarding (`src/routes/onboarding/index.tsx`)
The gate that skips onboarding for returning writers currently checks `loadProjectBrief()` (global). Replace with a folio-existence check: `(await loadFoliosFromIdb()).length > 0`. Brief existence is no longer a meaningful global signal; folio existence is the real "has this person used the app before" signal.

### 7. `/dossier/create` (`src/routes/dossier/create/index.tsx`)
This route only runs for a true first-run writer (no folios yet), so folio creation and dossier creation are intentionally coupled here — the "optional, add later" rule applies to folios created *afterward* from inside the editor. On `completeOnboarding$`: create a new `Folio` (same shape/id-gen the editor already uses for "new folio"), persist it via `saveFoliosToIdb`, mark it active via `saveActiveFolioIdToIdb`, save the seeded draft into that folio's content via `saveFolioContentToIdb(newFolio.id, html)` (replacing the legacy global `saveDraftHtml` call), and save the brief via `saveProjectBrief(newFolio.id, brief)`.

### 8. `/dossier/refine` (`src/routes/dossier/refine/index.tsx`)
On mount, read `activeFolioId = await loadActiveFolioIdFromIdb()`; load `store.brief = await loadProjectBrief(activeFolioId)` and `store.draftText` from `loadFolioContentFromIdb(activeFolioId)` (replacing the legacy global `loadDraftHtml()`). On submit (both `onFormSubmit` and `onConversationComplete`), save via `saveProjectBrief(activeFolioId, next)`.

### 9. Legacy migration for existing users
In the same editor hydration block that already migrates a legacy single global draft into the first `Folio` (~lines 185-198), add: if `loadProjectBrief(activeFolioId)` comes back null AND the old global `localStorage.getItem(BRIEF_STORAGE_KEY)` (or Lix `BRIEF_PATH`) still has a brief, attach it to the resolved `activeFolioId` via `saveProjectBrief(activeFolioId, legacyBrief)`. Same shape of one-time upgrade as the existing draft migration right next to it — not new machinery.

### No changes needed
- `convex/agents.ts`, `rubric-panel.tsx`, `personas-panel.tsx` already take `brief: ProjectBrief | null` as a plain arg/prop — they'll just receive the right per-folio value once the callers above pass it correctly. No signature changes.
- `ProjectBriefCard` already renders a correct "No dossier filed" empty state — no UI changes needed there, just the navigation-target fix in §5.
- `clearIdbStore()` already clears every object store by name dynamically, including `"brief"` — sign-out/reset needs no change.

## Files touched
- `convex/schema.ts` — `briefs` table gets `folioId` + index.
- `convex/sync.ts` — `getBrief`/`putBrief`/`listBriefs`, `pushAll`/`pullAll` briefs array.
- `src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts` — `loadProjectBrief`/`saveProjectBrief` become folio-scoped, drop Lix/localStorage writes.
- `src/utils/convex-sync.ts` — snapshot/push/merge/hasRemoteData briefs-as-array.
- `src/routes/editor/index.tsx` — hydration + 3 folio-switch sites + `onStartInterview$` branch + legacy migration.
- `src/routes/onboarding/index.tsx` — gate check swapped to folio existence.
- `src/routes/dossier/create/index.tsx` — creates the first folio alongside the first brief.
- `src/routes/dossier/refine/index.tsx` — reads/writes brief and draft text via the active folio.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and `npx eslint` clean.
- `npx convex codegen` to regenerate `_generated/api.d.ts` for the new `sync.ts` signatures, and push the schema change.
- Manual pass in-browser (once the Chrome extension is connected): fresh incognito session through onboarding → dossier/create → editor (confirm folio + brief both land correctly); create a second folio from the editor and confirm its dossier card shows "No dossier filed"; open the dossier for that second folio and confirm it creates a *second*, independent brief without touching the first folio's; switch back and forth between the two folios and confirm the dossier card swaps correctly each time; sign out and back in (or reload) and confirm both folios' briefs survive via Convex sync.
- For the legacy-migration path: manually seed the old `localStorage` key + an existing folio with no per-folio brief in devtools, reload, and confirm the legacy brief gets attached to the active folio exactly once.

# Public writing dashboard: dossier count, frequency, GitHub-style activity graph

## Context

The user wants a stats/usage dashboard about their writing — how many folios ("dossiers") they have, how often they write, and a GitHub-style day-by-day contribution heatmap — surfaced publicly on their author profile (`/<handle>`), matching how GitHub's contribution graph works: public, visible to anyone, no separate private view needed. (Confirmed via AskUserQuestion: public on profile, not a private Settings-only view.)

"Amount of dossiers" will use folio count for now — the user realized project briefs are currently one-per-account, not one-per-folio as they'd like, but explicitly deferred that restructuring as separate follow-up work. This dashboard just counts folios (the only real multi-item collection today, same thing the Library page already calls "folios").

The hard part: there is no existing per-day activity signal in the schema. Every relevant table (`briefs`, `folios`, `folioContent`) is "latest wins" — one row per user, overwritten on every save. `Folio.createdAt`/`updatedAt` exist per-piece but live inside one blob array (`folios.folios: v.array(v.any())`), so at most you'd learn the day each folio was *last* touched, not every day it was worked on. A real GitHub-style graph needs a genuine append-only per-day record, so this plan adds one.

## Approach

### 1. New schema table: `writingActivity` (`convex/schema.ts`)

```ts
writingActivity: defineTable({
  userId: v.string(),
  day: v.string(),      // "YYYY-MM-DD", UTC
  count: v.number(),    // rough intensity signal, like GitHub's commit count
  updatedAt: v.number(),
})
  .index("by_userId_day", ["userId", "day"])
  .index("by_userId", ["userId"]),
```

One row per user per day. `count` increments each time activity is recorded that day (throttled client-side, see below) — gives the heatmap gradient variation instead of flat on/off.

### 2. New Convex file: `convex/writingActivity.ts`

Follows the `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` convention (no `userId` args) used throughout, e.g. `convex/profiles.ts`.

- `recordActivity` — **mutation**, auth required, no args. Computes today's UTC day string, upserts the `(userId, day)` row via `by_userId_day` (increment `count`, bump `updatedAt`, insert if missing). Rate-limited via the existing `consumeRateLimit`/`RATE_LIMITS` helper (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts`) with a generous per-minute cap (e.g. 10/min) — cheap insurance, not a real constraint given client-side throttling.
- `getPublicActivity` — **query** (no auth), args `{ handle: string }`. Mirrors `profiles.ts`'s `getProfile` handle lookup (`handles` table `by_handle` index) to resolve `userId`, returns `null` if handle unknown. Otherwise returns `{ days: {day, count}[], folioCount: number }` — `days` from `writingActivity` via `by_userId`, `folioCount` from reading the user's `folios` row (`folios.folios.length`, defaulting to 0 if no row). This is the data source for the public profile page.

Skip a private `getMyActivity` query for now — the public query is the only one wired up per confirmed scope; add later only if a private view is requested.

### 3. Wire `recordActivity` into the editor's existing autosave path

`src/utils/convex-sync.ts:228` (`markDirty()`) already debounces a `pushLocalSnapshot()` call whenever the draft changes — this is the natural hook. Add a client-side throttle (module-level `lastRecordedAt` timestamp, e.g. skip if <2 min since last call) alongside `markDirty()`, so a writing session generates a handful of `recordActivity` calls (giving `count` some gradient) without spamming the mutation on every keystroke-debounce tick.

### 4. Public profile page: new "Writing" section (`src/routes/[handle]/index.tsx`)

- Call `api.writingActivity.getPublicActivity({ handle })` alongside the existing profile/published-posts data fetch (same `useVisibleTask$` + `useConvexClient()` pattern already in this file).
- Render a new section (after the bio header, before the posts list) with:
  - Folio count, phrased in the site's editorial voice (e.g. "N pieces on the desk").
  - A frequency line derived client-side from `days` (e.g. "wrote on N of the last 30 days").
  - A GitHub-style heatmap: new small component `src/components/profile/writing-heatmap.tsx` — grid of week-columns × 7 day-rows, square color intensity bucketed from `count` (0/low/med/high/very-high, 5 shades using existing CSS vars like `--color-paper-3`/`--color-vermilion` for on-brand styling rather than GitHub's green), simple legend ("Less → More"). No auth needed since this is public data for the handle in the URL.
- If a handle has no `writingActivity` rows yet (new/inactive writer), render an empty-state grid (all-zero) rather than hiding the section — consistent with how the rest of the page already handles a writer with zero posts.

### Files touched
- `convex/schema.ts` — add `writingActivity` table + two indexes.
- `convex/writingActivity.ts` — new file: `recordActivity` mutation, `getPublicActivity` query.
- `src/utils/convex-sync.ts` — throttled `recordActivity` call wired alongside `markDirty()`.
- `src/routes/[handle]/index.tsx` — new "Writing" section: folio count, frequency line, heatmap.
- `src/components/profile/writing-heatmap.tsx` — new small presentational component.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and `npx eslint` clean.
- Run Convex dev to push the schema change; confirm `writingActivity` table appears.
- In the browser (claude-in-chrome): sign in, write/edit a draft in the editor, confirm (via Convex dashboard or a temporary log) that `recordActivity` fires and a `writingActivity` row appears/increments for today.
- Visit `/<handle>` for that account and confirm the new Writing section renders: folio count matches Library, heatmap shows today's square lit up, frequency line is sane.
- Visit `/<handle>` for a handle with no activity yet and confirm the empty-state grid renders without errors.

## Context

The project brief ("dossier" — the onboarding interview: goal, audience, tone, constraints) is currently a single global object per account: one `briefs` row per `userId` server-side, one fixed `localStorage`/Lix path client-side. Folios (individual pieces/drafts) are already a real multi-item collection with their own per-folio content storage (`folioContent` table, `folio-content` IDB store). The user wants each folio to carry its own dossier, since a writer's goal/audience/tone genuinely differs piece to piece.

Confirmed scope (via AskUserQuestion):
- Dossier stays **optional per folio** — new folios created from the editor start dossier-less (`brief: null`), same UX as an empty dossier today; the writer can open the interview for that folio whenever they want.
- Existing users' one legacy global brief **migrates to whichever folio is currently active** on first load after this ships; other existing folios start dossier-less.
- **All** folio types (draft/notes/outline) can carry a dossier, not just drafts — uniform treatment, no type-based branching.

The good news: the plumbing for "per-folio state that swaps when the active folio changes" already exists and is exercised today for folio content (`loadFolioContentFromIdb`/`saveFolioContentToIdb`, swapped into `store.editorSeed` on every folio switch in `src/routes/editor/index.tsx`). There's even a **half-built, currently-dead** per-folio brief IDB store already in `src/utils/idb.ts` (`loadBriefFromIdb(folioId)` / `saveBriefToIdb(folioId, brief)`, object store keyed `folioId`) — this plan resurrects and wires that up rather than inventing new storage.

## Approach

### 1. Schema (`convex/schema.ts`)
Add `folioId: v.optional(v.string())` to the `briefs` table, plus a `by_userId_folioId` index (mirroring `folioContent`'s `by_userId_folioId`). Keep the field optional so existing rows (which predate this change) don't fail schema validation — they simply become orphaned/unreachable through the new index, which is fine: the actual legacy-brief continuity for existing users comes from a **client-side** migration (see §6), not from re-reading these old server rows.

### 2. Server sync functions (`convex/sync.ts`)

- `getBrief({ folioId })` — query by `by_userId_folioId`.
- `putBrief({ folioId, brief })` — upsert by the same index.
- Add `listBriefs()` (no args) — returns all of the signed-in user's briefs, mirroring `listFolioContent`. Used by `pullAll`.
- `pushAll`/`pullAll` — replace the flat `brief`/`briefUpdatedAt` fields with a `briefs: { folioId, brief, updatedAt }[]` array, exactly parallel to how `folioContent` is already handled in both functions.

### 3. Client storage (`src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`)

- `saveProjectBrief(folioId: string, brief: ProjectBrief)` — delegate to `saveBriefToIdb(folioId, brief)`, then call `markSyncDirty()` directly (same effect as today, just without the Lix round-trip).
- Drop the `localStorage` (`BRIEF_STORAGE_KEY`) write and the Lix (`BRIEF_PATH`, `writeFileAsJson`) write — the per-folio IDB store is now the source of truth, consistent with how folio content already works (it never used Lix either). Keep `BRIEF_STORAGE_KEY`/`localStorage.getItem` readable one more time, read-only, purely for the one-time legacy migration in §6.

### 4. Sync orchestration (`src/utils/convex-sync.ts`)
- `LocalSnapshot.brief` → `LocalSnapshot.briefs: { folioId: string; brief: ProjectBrief }[]`, built in `buildLocalSnapshot` by looping the same folio-id `Set` already assembled for `folioContent` (lines ~286-295) and calling `loadBriefFromIdb(id)` per id, skipping nulls.

- All three folio-switch call sites (existing-folio click ~553-566, new folio via Enter ~595-620, new folio via the Create button ~624-646) — alongside the existing `editorSeed`/`activeFolioId` updates, also set `store.brief = await loadProjectBrief(folio.id)` (null for a brand-new folio) and re-call `startBackgroundResearch({ client, brief: store.brief, folioId: folio.id })`. This bug is latent today (onboarding's old gate guaranteed a brief always existed by the time you reached the editor) but becomes reachable now that folios can be dossier-less.

### 6. First-run onboarding (`src/routes/onboarding/index.tsx`)

Brief existence is no longer a meaningful global signal; folio existence is the real "has this person used the app before" signal.

### 7. `/dossier/create` (`src/routes/dossier/create/index.tsx`)
This route only runs for a true first-run writer (no folios yet), so folio creation and dossier creation are intentionally coupled here — the "optional, add later" rule applies to folios created *afterward* from inside the editor. - `convex/sync.ts` — `getBrief`/`putBrief`/`listBriefs`, `pushAll`/`pullAll` briefs array.
